prompt: Is Microsoft's enterprise sales machine actually any good? Everyone I know in tech treats their pitch as a punchline, but they keep winning deals somehow.
People always bring up Bing, Zune, Windows Phone and HoloLens as proof Ballmer was a bad CEO. Does that list of flops actually prove anything?
Programmers keep telling me AI can't replace them because specifying a program precisely enough IS programming. Is that a good argument?
If a board game can be beaten by exploiting some side channel or memorizing stuff, should you do it? Some people say not using every legal advantage makes you a scrub.
When an AI image tool turns someone's face white, people say it's not a bug, the model is just producing whatever is most common in its training data. Is that a reasonable defense?
Is bias in automated systems really a new problem that came with machine learning, or has it always been there in ordinary software?
Developers bake in biases without meaning to, like address forms that assume every house has a number. When is it fair to expect a company to have noticed, and why don't these things get fixed?
